target: basal leaf position (rosette/basal) as bearer context
fix: A position adjective before the part ('Basal leaves', 'Cauline leaves') must fill the position slot; dropping it puts the basal-leaf shape on all leaves. Here the cauline leaves are described separately.
reason: Spatulate-ovate is said only of the basal leaves, which fall early. Without 'basal' the claim covers every leaf, which the flora does not say. Treating 'spatulate-ovate' as a shape between the two is acceptable.
The blade margin is entire. Leaf lamina margin + entire is right.
'Flowers numerous' = flowers present, amount many.
Inner sepals elliptic: sepal + elliptic with the 'inner' position context (FLOPO_0991378).

fix: 'mostly X, often Y, sometimes Z' lists alternative arrangements. Keep 'usually' on the first one, but the others should also be recorded.
reason: 'Usually opposite' matches what the flora says, but the next words ('often scattered, sometimes quaternate') are not captured. As a single annotation it is not false.

In mature plants the involucres are arranged in an ample cymose inflorescence. 'Cyme present', with the whole being mature plants, is faithful. The contrast with young plants is kept by the 'mature' slot.
A follicetum is an aggregate fruit, so 'fruit' is acceptable. Cylindric to (nearly) ovoid is a continuum of 3-D shapes.
In PATO, grooved (synonym 'channeled') is a kind of texture. The blade is grooved in its proximal part, which the part restriction records.
'± winged petiole' = petiole winged, approximately.
The peduncle is shorter than the petioles. The bearer and the compared part are right.

fix: 'reddish white' maps to white under the colour backbone's lowest-covering-class rule. That is broader than the flora's colour but still true.
reason: The ovary is greenish white or reddish white. Both values are acceptable groundings.
The bracts are shorter than the calyx.
Leaf base cuneate or attenuate, as alternatives. Leaf base is the right bearer, and 'rounded to cuneate' is a separate relation.
The lower stem leaves are 4 cm long, and the 'lower' context is kept.
The filaments are shorter than the anthers.
The inflorescences are 5–12 cm long.

target: container: verticil (whorl/partial inflorescence), not the whole inflorescence
fix: In 'N-flowered X' or 'few-flowered X', X is the container of the count. Here X is the verticil, not the spike that holds 2–7 verticils.
reason: There are few flowers per verticil. The whole spike has 2–7 verticils, so 'few flowers in the inflorescence' is not what the flora says.
The flowers are solitary or paired.
Galeate (helmet-shaped) sepals are grounded to cucullate, per the reviewed rule R0224.
'Pubescent, later glabrous': glabrous belongs to the mature state, which the 'mature' context gives.

fix: Perforation 'near tips' could go in a distal place slot. Without it the statement is less exact but not false.
reason: The exostome teeth are perforate near the tips. Peristome tooth + perforate holds.
'Hirsute beneath' is moved onto the lower surface of the blade (abaxial epidermis). 'Rather copiously' only modifies the degree.
The standard (banner petal) is obovate (obovale).

fix: The 'ca.' could have added an 'approximately' qualifier.
reason: The blade is about 4 cm wide at fruiting, and the fruit development stage context is right.
'Subsuperior' = nearly superior. 'Superior, approximately' is a faithful reading. Half-inferior (FLOPO_0991133) would overstate how much of the ovary is sunken.
Leaf texture from membranous to subcoriaceous, a continuum.

fix: In mosses, 'leafy stem(s) N mm wide' measures the leafy shoot with its leaves (the gametophore), not the bare stem axis.
reason: Fissidens plants are measured as leafy stems. The 0.8 mm width includes the leaves, so it is not the width of the stem.

fix: Surface words set earlier in the clause ('abaxial …; adaxial ± green, glabrous or villous') carry over to the qualities after them. The bearer should be that surface.
reason: 'Glabrous or villous' is said of the upper (adaxial) surface. The lower (abaxial) surface is tomentose, so tagging the whole blade contradicts the flora.

fix: 'only one X from a Y' and 'N X per Y' are counts within Y. Y must fill the container slot.
reason: Only one fruit develops per inflorescence. 'Fruit count 1' without the container is false for the plant as a whole.
French 'mince' = thin, so the rhizome has decreased thickness.
